summary: This is a sound stage 2 of the CUTLASS line that DIAGNOSIS action 3 explicitly owns. The one-M-tile 256x128 cooperative split-K design directly fixes stage 1's diagnosed tile-shape error and can physically reach M2 on pooler/unpooler/qkv. The builder must port it onto current master 36c26199, not 353e3b19, and re-baseline the pooler incumbent to master's NN-layout kernel. No companion run is needed.
justification: Mechanism: at m=256 the four rows sit near SGLang parity on nvjet (master 741072dc: qkv row 19.5/kernel 20.0, o 9.4/8.3, pooler 28.0/28.8 NNT, unpooler 24.2/24.8). Their compute floors are 9.8/4.5/17.4/17.4 us, so verify_32 holds about 25-40 us of headroom, which DIAGNOSIS ranks as the right place to spend. A 256x128x64 cooperative tile (2 consumer WGs x 128x128, 128 fp32 acc regs/thread, 4 x 48 KB stages fits under 227 KB) is the standard Hopper config. With static split-K giving 126-128 CTAs in one wave, the per-CTA compute floor is about 17.9 us for pooler (17.4 x 132/128). At a realistic 75-80% wgmma efficiency plus a 3-partial fixup and the ~0.9 us Memset node, that lands around 23-25 us. M2 (<= nvjet) is reachable and M3 is borderline but not impossible. qkv (18 x 7 = 126 CTAs, uneven 18-19 k-steps each, 6 partials per tile) lands around 13-16 us, also borderline at M3 15.5. Weakest link: the causal story that stage 1 lost because 'W was fetched twice by two M-tiles'. pooler at m=256 is near compute/DRAM balance (17.4 us compute vs about 14 us DRAM), and nvjet already uses 128-row tiles at 28.8 us, so the second M-tile's W read is probably largely an L2 hit. The real limiter is more likely mainloop efficiency plus the serialized split-K fixup plus the per-row Memset. Either way the profile will attribute it, because it is a rewrite judged on per-row kernel time. o is the weakest shape: k=1024 x 2 splits gives 8 k-steps per CTA against a 4-stage pipeline, so prologue/epilogue and the memset dominate, and it will likely miss M2 (8.3 us kernel). Stale numbers: the hypothesis quotes pooler as TNT 29.7 kernel / 31.3 row and base blob 353e3b19. Master has since landed pooler-nn-layout-widen-m256 (pooler m=256 is now nvjet 128x64 NNT 28.8 kernel / 28.0 row) and combo-rowowner (36c26199). The M2 bar for pooler must be 28.8, not 29.7. Prior: depends_on bf16-verify-streamk-cutlass-wgmma-rewrite (stage 1, regression 1.1635x, f5b1361a). The difference is real, not the same mechanism again: a 256-row single M-tile with N-multicast of x, and static SplitK to exactly one wave instead of 128x128 StreamK/Heuristic. It is not on any Do-not-try list. DIAGNOSIS's Do-not-try explicitly hands the m>=128 band to 'the CUTLASS line (action 3)'. Expected directions are consistent with TASK: only verify_32 is scored at m in 129..256; m=130/200 tests also take the path; all other loads should be flat.
confounders: pooler-nn-layout-widen-m256: this redefines the pooler m=129..256 incumbent as NN-layout nvjet 128x64 NNT (28.8 kernel / 28.0 row, flag nn_p256_ok). The CUTLASS route takes precedence over that path, so a pooler 'gain' must be judged against 28.8/28.0, not the hypothesis's TNT 29.7/31.3. With the stale bar, a 29.0 us CUTLASS kernel would read as an M2 pass while actually losing to master. state['pooler_t'] stays allocated either way, so this is a measurement confounder, not a functional one.

combo-rowowner-reduce-free-m1-qkv-o-plus-naive (current master 36c26199): this does not touch m=256, but the hypothesis says it is built on blob 353e3b19. If the builder ports onto the stale blob, every m<=128 row (bulk row-owner m=1, the qkv m=128 Lt B-cell) differs from master. Headline and non-target rows would then move for reasons unrelated to this change. It must be built on 36c26199 so the m<=256-excluded paths are byte-identical.

sglang-gemm-dispatch-parity: this is the fallback for qkv_gate/o/unpooler at m=256 and the DISABLED path. If any layer self-check fails, that row silently measures this incumbent. Grep [streamk] build OK / DISABLED / PATH CHOSEN before reading any per-row number (LESSONS: load_inline wgmma builds silently fall back without TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=9.0a and -std=c++20).

restack-three-cell-wins-router-unpooler-cluster-m8-nn-m128: the NN gate is 65..128 (NN_GATED_MAX_M=128), so it does not overlap 129..256 for unpooler. There is no interaction as long as the new gate starts at m >= 129. Verify that the test at m=130 does not double-route.
interference: No companion is warranted. This is a rewrite judged on the replaced kernels' own per-row time (profile top_kernels) against the incumbent and floor, and each of the four m=256 rows is attributable directly from one profile because the gate is 129 <= m <= 256 only. Every other path is byte-identical to master when built on 36c26199. The only landed interaction (the pooler NN layout) is a re-baselining issue, fixed by quoting the right incumbent, not by an ab-revert. Reverting it would only make the bar easier and the result less meaningful. The one sub-change that is ambiguous is split-K fixup + memset cost vs mainloop/tile-shape cost. That is best answered for free inside this run by the prepare-time print-only cold-L2 timings (add a splits=1 variant per layer, especially o and unpooler, alongside the chosen split). A separate check would spend a run on it. In-flight pooler-k-halves-fp32-partials-restack-m128-m256 and the DIAGNOSIS action-2 per-cell cuBLAS selector would move the pooler/qkv/o/unpooler m=256 incumbents if they land first. Whichever lands second must be re-measured against the new master, and a restack decision should be per cell.
rules_flags: None blocking. The workspace is allocated in prepare(); the split-K barrier Memset is a captured graph node on the current stream (fine, but count it in the row). Routing branches only on cfg layer/m/n and shapes. bf16 out with fp32 accumulate and fp32 split-K partials keeps the weights at native precision. The prepare-time timing is print-only.

Make sure every host-side CUTLASS step in kernel_fn (Arguments build, can_implement, get_workspace_size, the grid<=132 assert) depends only on shapes, never on tensor values, and that no cudaDeviceSynchronize/cudaGetLastError-with-sync slips into the timed path. Put the grid assert and can_implement in prepare().

The split-K reduction must be deterministic (CUTLASS ReductionMode::Deterministic, or the SplitK fixup order fixed) so that the run2 bit-identical self-check holds. A nondeterministic reduction is not a rule break at 1% rel-L2, but it would make the self-check flaky and could disable the path.
open_questions: Does the CUTLASS sm90 stream-K/SplitK tile scheduler accept ClusterShape 1x2x1 with static splits=7 for qkv (18 N-tiles, uneven K of 128 k-steps / 7) and still give exactly 126 CTAs? Print can_implement, the grid and the applied decomposition, and assert the grid in prepare.

For o (k=1024, 8 k-steps per split) and possibly unpooler, would splits=1 (64 CTAs, no workspace, no Memset node) beat splits=2? Print both in prepare's cold-L2 replay so stage 3 can choose per layer without another run.

Can the per-row Memset node (~0.9 us x 4 rows ≈ 3.6 us on a ~91 us verify_32 load, about 4%) be removed, for example by self-resetting barrier counters in the epilogue? Per LESSONS, deleting a graph node can matter as much as kernel speed. Record its cost separately as planned.

Should the pooler M2 bar be restated as <= 28.8 kernel / 28.0 row (master NN layout), and the qkv bar as master's 20.0 kernel / 19.5 row rather than stage 1's 25.3? 'qkv not worse than stage 1' is too weak a bar for promotion.

Ordering vs DIAGNOSIS actions 1-2: if the pooler K-halves restack (26.75 row) or the per-cell cuBLAS selector lands first, the pooler/qkv incumbents drop. Promotion should then be per cell against that newer master, and should follow the new LESSONS rule (two interleaved rounds >= 1.03 with an IQR bound) for any prepare-time selector that gates the CUTLASS path.
